title: Estimated costs reconcile against the actual AWS bill
description:
Everything else in this epic produces estimates. An estimate nobody ever
checks becomes wrong quietly -- a rate change, a region change, an instance
type change, or a provisioning allowance that was always too low, and the
console reports confident figures that drift further from the invoice every
month.

Pull the actual daily cost from Cost Explorer and store it beside the summed
estimate. The delta is the product: it tells the operator how far to trust the
per-job numbers, and it tells us when the rate card needs updating.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Reconciling estimated cost against actual AWS cost

  Scenario: Actual daily cost is recorded alongside the estimate
    Given estimated costs exist for a day
    When the reconciliation runs for that day
    Then the day records an actual cost from AWS
    And the day records the variance against the estimate

  Scenario: Reconciliation waits for AWS cost data to settle
    Given a day that ended two hours ago
    When the reconciliation runs
    Then that day is not reconciled

  Scenario: Operator sees estimate and actual together
    Given a reconciled day exists
    When the operator requests the cost summary
    Then the summary reports both estimated and actual cost

  Scenario: A large variance is surfaced
    Given a reconciled day whose actual cost exceeds the estimate by more than the variance threshold
    When the operator requests the cost summary
    Then that day is flagged as out of tolerance
```

## Implementation brief

**Scheduled Lambda** -- EventBridge rule, once daily, reconciling the day that
closed at least 24 hours ago. Cost Explorer data is not final immediately;
reconciling too early produces a variance that is just latency.

**`ce:GetCostAndUsage`** with `Granularity=DAILY`, grouped by `SERVICE`, or
filtered by a cost allocation tag. Be aware:

- Cost Explorer charges roughly 0.01 USD per API request. One call per day is
  negligible; a call per page load would not be. Never call it from a request
  path -- only from the scheduled job, writing results to the rollup table.
- Cost allocation tags must be activated in the billing console before they
  appear in Cost Explorer, and activation is not retroactive. If tag-based
  attribution is wanted, tag the Batch compute resources in CDK **and**
  document the manual activation step, because a deployer who skips it gets
  silently empty results rather than an error.
- The AWS account may run more than Auritus. Filtering by service alone will
  attribute unrelated EC2 spend to Auritus. Tag-based filtering is the correct
  answer; service filtering is acceptable only for a dedicated account, and
  the docs must say which assumption is in force.

**Storage** -- extend the rollup records with `actual_cost_usd`,
`reconciled_at`, and `variance_usd`. Reconciliation is account-wide while
rollups are per-site, so actuals land on a distinct account-level rollup key
rather than being split across sites by a guess. Per-site actual cost is not
obtainable from Cost Explorer and should not be fabricated.

**`variance_threshold_percent`** -- CDK context, for the out-of-tolerance flag.

## Blocked on

The daily cost rollups story, which owns the records this extends.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented on feature/cost-reconciliation, merged to develop. New scheduled Lambda (daily cron, 06:00 UTC) reconciles the most recent Cost-Explorer-final day (closed >=24h ago) plus any earlier day in a bounded 7-day lookback still missing reconciled_at -- self-healing a missed run without unbounded rescanning. Account-wide actual cost written via SET (not ADD -- a deterministic fact, not an accumulated contribution, correctly reasoned as naturally idempotent) to a sentinel __account__ row in the same AuritusCostRollups table. Filtered to EC2+Batch services only (the volatile GPU-cost side of the rate card; platform cost is already a flat estimate) with the single-dedicated-account attribution assumption stated explicitly in the module docstring, not silently assumed. Response-shape decision: a new additive 'reconciliation' key on GET /admin/costs rather than folding the sentinel into 'daily' -- verified this doesn't pollute daily's per-site sums, since the router explicitly excludes the sentinel from daily before computing total. Zero-estimate edge case reasoned correctly: zero estimate + nonzero actual flags out-of-tolerance (a real signal, not a divide-by-zero to hide) while zero-vs-zero is perfect agreement. CLI and console both extended additively, confirmed non-breaking for pre-existing tests. Independently re-verified across all three suites this touches: cli (black/ruff/pytest 72 passed/behave 30 features 118 scenarios), cdk (49 pytest passed, synth clean), console (lint/tsc clean, actual Playwright run 25/25 passing including every pre-existing spec). No fixes needed in review -- this was clean, well-reasoned work throughout.
